title.zh: 卷八十七 列傳第四十七 蕭惠開 殷琰
title.en: Volume 87 Biographies 47: Xiao Huikai, Yin Yan
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第四十七 蕭惠開 殷琰 Volume 87 Biographies 47: Xiao Huikai, Yin Yan

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十七 蕭惠開 殷琰

translations.literal: Biographies 47: Xiao Huikai, Yin Yan
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 47: Xiao Huikai and Yin Yan

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開，南蘭陵人，征西將軍思話子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai was a man of Nan Lanling, son of the General Who Pacifies the West, Xiao Sihua.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huikai, a native of Nan Lanling, was the son of Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 初名慧開，後改慧為惠。

translations.literal: His original name was Huikai; later he changed Hui to Hui (as in favor/benefit).
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Huikai; later he changed the character hui (clever) to hui (kindness).

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，涉獵文史，家雖貴戚，而居服簡素。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and bearing, ranged widely through literature and history; though his family was an eminent kinship group, in dress and conduct he was plain and simple.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he had force of character and read widely in letters and history. Though his clan was among the great affinal kin, he dressed and lived simply.

sentences.zh: 初為秘書郎，著作並名家年少。

translations.literal: He first served as Secretariat Gentleman, among the young men of famous families in the Secretariat and Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Secretariat Gentleman, one of the gifted young men attached to the Secretariat and the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 惠開意趣與人多不同，比肩或三年不共語。

translations.literal: Huikai's bent differed greatly from others'; side by side with colleagues he might go three years without speaking together.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai's temperament set him far apart from others; he might stand beside a colleague for three years without exchanging a word.

sentences.zh: 外祖光祿大夫沛郡劉成戒之曰：「汝恩戚家子，當應將迎時俗，緝外內之歡。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather, Liu Cheng of Pei commandery, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, admonished him, saying: "You are the son of an enfeoffed kinship house; you ought to meet the fashion of the times and knit together joy within and without.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Liu Cheng of Pei, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, warned him: "As a son of an imperial affinal house, you should court the customs of the day and bind up goodwill inside and outside the clan.

sentences.zh: 如汝自業，將無小傷多異，以取天下之疾患邪？」

translations.literal: If you persist in your own course, will you not by many small hurts and many oddities draw the world's maladies upon yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: If you keep to your own way, will you not, by countless petty frictions and eccentricities, bring the world's resentment down on your head?"

sentences.zh: 惠開曰：「人間宜相緝和，甚如慈旨。

translations.literal: Huikai said: "Among men one ought indeed to knit harmony together, very much as your kindly instruction says.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai replied: "It is true that men ought to live in mutual harmony, exactly as your gracious counsel urges.

sentences.zh: 但不幸耿介，恥見作凡人，畫龍未成，故遂至於多忤耳。」

translations.literal: But unhappily I am upright and unyielding; I am ashamed to be taken for an ordinary man. The dragon is not yet finished in the painting, and so I have come to so many clashes."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am unhappily stiff-necked by nature and cannot bear to be counted a common man. The dragon is still unfinished on the wall—that is why I offend so often."

sentences.zh: 轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 與汝南周朗同官友善，以偏奇相尚。

translations.literal: With Zhou Lang of Runan he served in the same office on friendly terms, each prizing the other's eccentric brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: He became close with Zhou Lang of Runan, who held the same post; the two admired each other's unconventional genius.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書水部郎，始興王濬征北府主簿，南徐州治中從事史，徙汝陰王友；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, Water Section; chief clerk in the Pacifying-North headquarters of Prince Jun of Shixing; Registrar and Assistant Officer of the Secretariat of the Southern Inspectorate of Xu; then moved to Companion of the Prince of Ruyin;
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, Water Section; chief clerk on Prince Jun of Shixing's Pacifying-North staff; Registrar of the Southern Xu inspectorate; and Companion to the Prince of Ruyin;

sentences.zh: 又為南徐州別駕，中書侍郎，江夏王義恭大將軍大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: he also served as Vice-Director of the Southern Xu inspectorate, Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, and Assistant in the Bureau of the Grand Marshal and Grand General under Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: and later as Vice-Director of Southern Xu, Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, and staff officer on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's Grand Marshal and Grand General council.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，自太子中庶子轉黃門侍郎，與侍中何偃爭積射將軍徐沖之事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, he moved from Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and disputed with the Attendant-in-Ordinary He Yan over the case of the Rapid-Fire General Xu Chong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xiaojian era he was promoted from Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and clashed with Attendant-in-Ordinary He Yan over the dismissal of Rapid-Fire General Xu Chong.

sentences.zh: 偃任遇甚隆，惠開不為之屈，偃怒，使門下推彈之。

translations.literal: Yan's appointment and favor were very exalted; Huikai would not yield to him. Yan grew angry and had the Secretariat investigate and impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan enjoyed extraordinary favor at court, but Huikai refused to bow to him. Enraged, Yan ordered the Secretariat to investigate and impeach him.

sentences.zh: 惠開乃上表解職曰：「陛下未照臣愚，故引參近侍。

translations.literal: Huikai then submitted a memorial resigning his post, saying: "Your Majesty has not yet discerned my dullness, and so drew me among your close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai thereupon memorialized to resign, writing: "Your Majesty, not yet seeing how slow-witted I am, drew me into your intimate service.

sentences.zh: 臣以職事非長，故委能何偃，凡諸當否，不敢參議。

translations.literal: As I am not skilled in my duties, I entrusted competence to He Yan; in all matters of right and wrong I did not dare to join deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Finding myself unfit for the work, I left matters to the capable He Yan and did not venture to debate what was right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 竊見積射將軍徐沖之為偃命所黜，臣愚懷謂有可申，故聊設微異。

translations.literal: I privately saw that Rapid-Fire General Xu Chong was removed at Yan's order; in my foolish view there was ground to appeal, and so I ventured a slight dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I saw that Rapid-Fire General Xu Chong had been cashiered on Yan's orders; it seemed to my humble judgment that the case could be reopened, and I offered a modest objection.

sentences.zh: 偃恃恩使貴，欲使人靡二情，便訶脅主者。

translations.literal: Yan, relying on favor, acted as envoy of the exalted; wishing to leave men no second loyalty, he at once berated and threatened the chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, trusting in imperial grace, played the grand delegate; wanting no divided loyalty, he immediately hectored and intimidated the chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 手定文案，割落臣議，專載己辭。

translations.literal: With his own hand he fixed the document, cut away my deliberation, and recorded only his own wording.
translations.idiomatic: He personally revised the draft, struck out my comments, and entered only his own language.

sentences.zh: 雖天照廣臨，竟未見察臣理，違顏咫尺，致茲壅濫，則臣之受劾，蓋何足悲。

translations.literal: Though heaven's illumination is broad, in the end my reasoning was not perceived; with your countenance a foot away, this obstruction arose—then for me to be impeached is scarcely worth grief.
translations.idiomatic: Though heaven's light shines wide, my argument was never seen; with Your Majesty's face within a pace, such blockage arose—if I am punished for that, I can hardly call it tragic.

sentences.zh: 但不順侍中，臣有其咎，當而行之，不知何過。

translations.literal: But in not yielding to the Attendant-in-Ordinary I have my fault; when it should be done I do not know what offense it is.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if fault lies in not yielding to the Attendant-in-Ordinary, I own it; when the act was required, I do not know what crime was committed.

sentences.zh: 且議之不允，未有彈科，省心揆天，了知在宥。

translations.literal: Moreover, the deliberation was not approved, yet there was no impeachment statute; reflecting on my heart against heaven, I clearly know I am within pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the discussion was not adopted, but no charge was framed; weighing my heart against heaven, I know full well I stand within forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 臣不能謝愆右職，改意重臣，刺骨鑠金，將在朝夕。

translations.literal: I cannot apologize for fault in my rightful office and change my mind before a great minister; bone-piercing, metal-melting slander will come within days.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot atone in office while bending before a powerful minister; calumny sharp enough to pierce bone and melt metal will arrive any day.

sentences.zh: 乞解所忝，保拙私庭。」

translations.literal: I beg to be released from the post I disgrace and to keep my clumsiness in my private household."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be relieved of the post I dishonor and to guard my awkward self within my own gates."

sentences.zh: 時偃寵方隆，由此忤旨，別敕有司以屬疾多，免惠開官。

translations.literal: At that time Yan's favor was just at its height; by this Huikai offended the imperial intent. A separate edict ordered the authorities, on the ground of many dependents' illnesses, to dismiss Huikai from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's influence was then at its peak; Huikai had offended the throne. A special edict directed the authorities to remove him from office on the pretext that too many of his household were ill.

sentences.zh: 思話素恭謹，操行與惠開不同，常以其峻異，每加嫌責。

translations.literal: Sihua was by nature always respectful and cautious; his conduct differed from Huikai's, and he often blamed him for his harsh strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had always been reverent and cautious; his ways differed from Huikai's, and he often reproached his son for harsh eccentricity.

sentences.zh: 及見惠開自解表，自歎曰：「兒子不幸與周朗周旋，理應如此。」

translations.literal: When he saw Huikai's memorial of self-dismissal he sighed to himself: "The boy was unfortunate enough to keep company with Zhou Lang; it had to turn out like this."
translations.idiomatic: When he read Huikai's resignation he sighed: "The boy was ill-fated to consort with Zhou Lang; no wonder it came to this."

sentences.zh: 杖之二百。

translations.literal: He had him beaten two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beaten two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 尋重除中庶子。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reappointed Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，居喪有孝性，家素事佛，凡為父起四寺，南岸南岡下，名曰禪岡寺；

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning with filial devotion. The family had long served the Buddha; in all he raised four temples for his father: below the southern ridge on the south bank, named Chan Ridge Temple;
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he mourned with true filial piety. The household had long been Buddhist; for his father he founded four temples: below the southern hill on the south bank, called Chan Ridge Temple;

sentences.zh: 曲阿舊鄉宅，名曰禪鄉寺；

translations.literal: at the old family residence in Qu'a, named Chan Village Temple;
translations.idiomatic: at the ancestral home in Qu'a, Chan Village Temple;

sentences.zh: 京口墓亭，名曰禪亭寺；

translations.literal: at the tomb pavilion in Jingkou, named Chan Pavilion Temple;
translations.idiomatic: at the grave pavilion in Jingkou, Chan Pavilion Temple;

sentences.zh: 所封封陽縣，名曰禪封寺。

translations.literal: in his enfeoffed territory of Fengyang county, named Chan Feng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: and in his fief of Fengyang county, Chan Feng Temple.

sentences.zh: 謂國僚曰：「封秩蓋鮮，而兄弟甚多，若使全關一人，則在我所讓。

translations.literal: He told the state retainers: "The fief income is rather slight, yet brothers are many; if the whole grant were given to one man, that would be my own renunciation.
translations.idiomatic: He told his fief staff: "The enfeoffment yields little, and my brothers are numerous. If one man took the whole income, that would be my own surrender of share.

sentences.zh: 若使人人等分，又事可悲恥。

translations.literal: If each were given an equal portion, the matter would again be pitiful and shameful.
translations.idiomatic: If everyone received an equal slice, the thing would be both pitiful and shameful.

sentences.zh: 寺眾既立，自宜悉供僧眾。」

translations.literal: Now that the temple communities are established, they should all be supplied to the monastic assembly."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the temples stand, the revenue ought to go entirely to the monks."

sentences.zh: 由此國秩不復下均。

translations.literal: From this the state stipend was no longer distributed equally below.
translations.idiomatic: After that the fief stipend was no longer divided among the household.

sentences.zh: 服除，除司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出為海陵王休茂北中郎長史、寧朔將軍、襄陽太守，行雍州州府事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he went out as Chief Clerk to Prince Xiumao of Hailing, General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, acting in the Yong provincial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he went out as chief clerk to Prince Xiumao of Hailing, General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, with acting charge of the Yong provincial government.

sentences.zh: 善於為政，威行禁止。

translations.literal: He was skilled in government; authority went forth and prohibitions were enforced.
translations.idiomatic: He governed well; his authority was felt and his bans obeyed.

sentences.zh: 襲封封陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Fengyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Fengyang county.

sentences.zh: 還為新安王子鸞冠軍長史，行吳郡事。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Champion Chief Clerk to Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, with acting charge of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Champion Chief Clerk to Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, acting as prefect of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 惠開妹當適桂陽王休範，女又當適世祖子，發遣之資，應須二千萬。

translations.literal: Huikai's younger sister was to marry Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, and his daughter was also to marry a son of the Emperor; the expenses of sending them off would require twenty million.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister was to marry Prince Xiufan of Guiyang and his daughter a son of the reigning emperor; their send-off would cost some twenty million cash.

sentences.zh: 乃以為豫章內史，聽其肆意聚納，由是在郡著貪暴之聲。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Interior Governor of Yuzhang and allowed to gather wealth as he pleased; on this account while in the commandery he gained a reputation for greedy violence.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made Interior Governor of Yuzhang and allowed to levy as he saw fit; in the commandery he earned a name for grasping cruelty.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書吏部郎，不拜，徙御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel but did not accept the post; he was moved to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel but declined the appointment and was transferred to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 世祖與劉秀之詔曰：「今以蕭惠開為憲司，冀當稱職。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote to Liu Xiuzhi: "We now appoint Xiao Huikai to the inspectorate, hoping he will suit the office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote to Liu Xiuzhi: "We now set Xiao Huikai over the inspectorate and expect him to fill the role.

sentences.zh: 但一往服領，已自殊有所震。」

translations.literal: Yet with a single previous tour of duty he has already made himself unusually imposing."
translations.idiomatic: But even one prior tour in office has already set people unusually on edge."

sentences.zh: 及在任，百僚畏憚之。

translations.literal: When he took up the post, all officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in post, every officer in the bureaucracy feared him.

sentences.zh: 八年，入為侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered court as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「惠開前在憲司，奉法直繩，不阿權戚，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Huikai, while in the inspectorate, upheld the law with a straight cord and did not flatter powerful kin; We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "While Imperial Censor, Huikai enforced the law impartially and did not court powerful families; We praise this highly.

sentences.zh: 可更授御史中丞。」

translations.literal: He may again be given the post of Imperial Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Let him again be appointed Imperial Censor."

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起為持節、督青冀二州諸軍事、輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史，不行。

translations.literal: When called back he was made Commissioner with Insignia, Commander of the military affairs of Qing and Ji provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Qing and Ji; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled to service he was made Commissioner with Insignia, commander of Qing and Ji, General Who Assists the State, and inspector of both provinces, but he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 改督益、寧二州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of Yi and Ning, with insignia and rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: His commission was changed to Yi and Ning, with the same insignia and rank.

sentences.zh: 惠開素有大志，至蜀，欲廣樹經略，善於述事，對賓僚及士人說收牂牁、越巂以為內地，綏討蠻、濮，闢地徵租；

translations.literal: Huikai had long cherished great designs; reaching Shu he wished to extend strategy broadly, was skilled in exposition, and told guests, staff, and local gentlemen of recovering Zangge and Yuexi as inner territories, pacifying the Man and Pu, opening land and levying tax;
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had long nursed grand ambitions. In Shu he meant to widen imperial strategy, was eloquent in counsel, and told retainers and local scholars of recovering Zangge and Yuexi as heartland territory, of pacifying the Man and Pu tribes, opening new lands and collecting tribute;

sentences.zh: 聞其言者，以為大功可立。

translations.literal: those who heard his words thought great achievement could be established.
translations.idiomatic: those who listened believed magnificent deeds lay within reach.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進號冠軍將軍，又進平西將軍，改督為都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Huikai was advanced to General Who Establishes the Army, then to General Who Pacifies the West, and his "command" was changed to "governor."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong succeeded, Huikai was promoted to General Who Establishes the Army and then to General Who Pacifies the West, and his commission was retitled from commander to governor.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛反，惠開乃集將佐謂之曰：「湘東太祖之昭，晉安世祖之穆，其於當璧，並無不可。

translations.literal: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled, Huikai gathered his aides and said to them: "Prince Dong of Xiang is a son of Taizong by the primary consort; Prince Jin'an is a son of the late Emperor by the secondary consort—for holding the jade disk either would do.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rose in rebellion, Huikai assembled his staff and said: "Prince Dong of Xiang is Taizong's son by the main house; Prince Jin'an is the late emperor's son by the consort branch—either could legitimately receive the realm.

sentences.zh: 但景和雖昏，本是世祖之嗣，不任社稷，其次猶多。

translations.literal: But although Emperor Jinghe was benighted, he was still the late Emperor's heir; he could not bear the altars of state, yet there were still many next in line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jinghe was muddled, yet he remained the late emperor's heir; unfit for the throne, there were still others ahead.

sentences.zh: 吾奉武、文之靈，兼荷世祖之眷，今便當投袂萬里，推奉九江。」

translations.literal: I, bearing the spirits of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen and also owing the late Emperor's grace, will now throw up my sleeves and go ten thousand li to advance and support Jiujiang."
translations.idiomatic: I carry the shades of Emperors Wu and Wen and the late emperor's favor alike; I shall now gird myself and march ten thousand li to set up Jiujiang."

sentences.zh: 乃遣巴郡太守費欣壽領二千人東下，為巴東人任叔兒起義所邀，欣壽敗沒，陝口道不復通。

translations.literal: He then sent the Administrator of Ba commandery, Fei Xinshou, east with two thousand men; they were waylaid by Ren Shuer of Ba commandery who raised righteous troops; Xinshou was defeated and lost, and the Shaan pass road was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Fei Xinshou, governor of Ba, eastward with two thousand men; Ren Shuer of Ba rose in loyalist revolt and ambushed him. Xinshou was destroyed, and the route through Shaan Pass was severed.

sentences.zh: 更遣州治中程法度領三千人步出梁州，又為氐賊楊僧嗣所斷。

translations.literal: He further sent the provincial Registrar Cheng Fadu with three thousand men on foot out through Liang province, but they were again cut off by the Di bandit Yang Sengsi.
translations.idiomatic: He next sent the provincial registrar Cheng Fadu with three thousand foot soldiers toward Liang, but the Di chieftain Yang Sengsi blocked them.

sentences.zh: 先是，惠開為治，多任刑誅，蜀土咸懷猜怨。

translations.literal: Earlier, in governing, Huikai had relied much on punishments and executions; all in Shu harbored suspicion and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Huikai had governed chiefly through harsh punishment; the people of Shu nursed suspicion and hate.

sentences.zh: 及聞欣壽沒，法度又不得前，晉原一郡遂反，於是諸郡悉應之，並來圍城。

translations.literal: When they heard that Xinshou had perished and Fadu could not advance, Jinyuan commandery rose at once; then every commandery answered and came to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xinshou was dead and Fadu could not get through, Jinyuan rebelled; every commandery followed, and all marched to encircle the capital.

sentences.zh: 城內東兵不過二千，凡蜀人惠開疑之，皆悉遣出。

translations.literal: Within the walls the eastern soldiers numbered no more than two thousand; all Shu natives whom Huikai distrusted he sent out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city the eastern troops were fewer than two thousand; every man of Shu whom Huikai doubted was expelled.

sentences.zh: 子勛尋平，蜀人並欲屠城，以望厚賞。

translations.literal: Before long Zixun was pacified; the Shu people all wished to sack the city for the hope of rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Zixun was crushed; the Shu people all wanted to slaughter the city for lavish bounty.

sentences.zh: 惠開每遣軍出戰，未嘗不捷，前後所摧破殺傷不可勝計。

translations.literal: Whenever Huikai sent troops out to fight he never failed to win; before and after, those broken, crushed, wounded, and killed were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent troops out they never returned defeated; the enemy broken, crushed, wounded, and slain were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 外眾逾合，勝兵者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: The outer hosts gathered ever thicker; their able warriors numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The besieging hosts swelled; their fighting men passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 時天下已平，太宗以蜀土險遠，赦其誅責，遣惠開弟惠基步道使蜀，具宣朝旨。

translations.literal: By then the realm was pacified; Taizong, because Shu was rugged and remote, pardoned the charge against him and sent Huikai's younger brother Huikai on foot as envoy to Shu to proclaim the court's intent fully.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was already at peace; Taizong, considering Shu remote and steep, forgave the indictment and sent Huikai's brother Huikai overland to announce the full court decree.

sentences.zh: 惠基既至涪，而蜀人志在屠城，不欲使王命遠達，遏留惠基不聽進。

translations.literal: When Huikai reached Fu, the Shu people's hearts were set on sacking the city and they did not wish the king's command to reach far; they detained Huikai and would not let him advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu the Shu men still meant to sack Chengdu and did not want the imperial message to arrive; they held Huikai back and refused him passage.

sentences.zh: 惠基率部曲破其渠帥馬興懷等，然後得前。

translations.literal: Huikai led his personal troops, broke the chieftain Ma Xinghuai and others, and only then was able to go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai broke the band of Ma Xinghuai and the other leaders with his own following, and only then pressed on.

sentences.zh: 惠開奉旨歸順，城圍得解。

translations.literal: Huikai received the order and submitted; the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai accepted the amnesty and submitted; the encirclement dissolved.

sentences.zh: 時太宗遣惠開宗人寶首水路慰勞益州，寶首欲以平蜀為功。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong had sent Huikai's clansman Baoshou by water to comfort Yi province; Baoshou wished to make the pacification of Shu his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had also sent their kinsman Baoshou by river to console Yi province; Baoshou hoped to win credit by finishing the pacification himself.

sentences.zh: 更獎說蜀人，於是處處蜂起，凡諸離散者，一時還合。

translations.literal: He further urged the Shu people on, and then everywhere they swarmed up; all who had dispersed at once gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: He stirred the Shu people anew until revolt flared everywhere; every scattered band reunited at once.

sentences.zh: 渠帥趙燕、句文章等，與寶首屯軍於上，去成都六十里，眾號二十萬人。

translations.literal: The chieftains Zhao Yan, Gou Wenzhang, and others camped with Baoshou above the city, sixty li from Chengdu, their host proclaimed at two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains Zhao Yan, Gou Wenzhang, and others joined Baoshou in camp sixty li above Chengdu, claiming two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 惠開欲遣擊之，將佐咸曰：「攻破蜀賊，誠不為難。

translations.literal: Huikai wished to send troops to strike them; the aides all said: "To break the Shu rebels would truly not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai meant to attack them, but his officers said: "Beating the Shu rebels would not be difficult.

sentences.zh: 但慰勞使至，未獲奉受，而遣兵相距，何以自明本心。」

translations.literal: But the comforting envoy has arrived and We have not yet received his charge; to send troops against him—how may We show Our true heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial comforter has come and we have not yet received his orders; if we fight him now, how will we prove our loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 惠開曰：「今水陸四斷，表啟路絕，寶首或相誣陷，謂我不奉朝旨。

translations.literal: Huikai said: "Now land and water are cut in four directions; memorials and reports have no road. Baoshou may slander and trap Us, saying We do not obey the court.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai said: "Land and water are blocked on every side; no memorial can get through. Baoshou may accuse me of defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 我之欲戰，本在通使；

translations.literal: Our wish to fight is originally in order to open the way for the envoy;
translations.idiomatic: I fight precisely to clear a path for the envoy;

sentences.zh: 使若得通，則誠心達矣。」

translations.literal: if the envoy can get through, then Our sincere heart will have reached them."
translations.idiomatic: once he passes, my loyalty will be plain."

sentences.zh: 乃作啟事，具陳事情，使腹心二人帶啟，戒之曰：「須賊破路開，便躍馬馳去。」

translations.literal: He then drafted a memorial detailing the situation, gave it to two trusted men to carry, and warned them: "When the rebels are broken and the road opens, leap on horseback and flee."
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a full report of events, gave it to two trusted men, and charged them: "When the enemy breaks and the road opens, spur your horses and ride."

sentences.zh: 遣永寧太守蕭惠訓、別駕費欣業萬兵並進，與戰，大破之，生禽寶首，囚於成都縣獄。

translations.literal: He sent the Administrator of Yongning, Xiao Huixun, and the Vice-Director Fei Xinye with ten thousand troops together; in battle they won a great victory, captured Baoshou alive, and imprisoned him in the Chengdu county jail.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Administrator Xiao Huixun of Yongning and Vice-Director Fei Xinye with ten thousand men; they won a crushing victory, took Baoshou alive, and jailed him in Chengdu county.

sentences.zh: 所遣使至，上使執送寶首，除惠開晉平王休祐驃騎長史、南郡太守，不拜。

translations.literal: When the envoy he had sent arrived, the court had Baoshou escorted to the capital; Huikai was made Champion Chief Clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Jinping and Administrator of Nan commandery, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his messenger arrived, the throne ordered Baoshou sent to the capital; Huikai was offered champion chief clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Jinping and prefect of Nan, but declined.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，還至京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，惠開府錄事參軍到希微負蜀人債將百萬，為責主所制，未得俱還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huikai's Registrar Dao Xihui owed the Shu people nearly a million in debt; the creditors held him and he could not return together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his registrar Dao Xihui owed the Shu nearly a million in cash; creditors detained him and he could not leave with the staff.

sentences.zh: 惠開與希微共事不厚，以為隨其同上，不能攜接得還，意恥之。

translations.literal: Huikai had not been close to Xihui in shared service; he thought that because Xihui followed him to the capital he could not bring him back—a matter of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had never been close to him; he felt ashamed that a man who had followed him upstream could not be brought home.

sentences.zh: 廄中凡有馬六十匹，悉以乞希微償責，其意趣不常皆如是。

translations.literal: In the stables there were sixty horses in all; he gave them all to Xihui to pay the debt; his bent was invariably such.
translations.idiomatic: He had sixty horses in the stable and gave every one to Xihui to settle the debt—his temper was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 先劉瑀為益州，張悅代之，瑀去任，凡所攜將佐有不樂反者，必逼制將還。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Yu had been in Yi province; when Zhang Yue replaced him, Yu on leaving took along every aide who was unwilling to rebel and forced them to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu had governed Yi, Zhang Yue succeeded him; on leaving, Yu forced every reluctant subordinate to march back with him.

sentences.zh: 語人曰：「隨我上，豈可為張悅作西門客邪！」

translations.literal: He told people: "If you follow me upstream, how can you become Zhang Yue's western-gate guest?"
translations.idiomatic: He told them: "You came upriver with me—will you now be Zhang Yue's gate guest on the west side?"

sentences.zh: 惠開自蜀還，資財二千餘萬，悉散施道路，一無所留。

translations.literal: When Huikai returned from Shu his assets exceeded twenty million; he gave it all away along the road and kept nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Shu with more than twenty million in goods, Huikai scattered it all along the road and kept none.

sentences.zh: 五年，又除桂陽王休範征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again made Champion Chief Clerk to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang and Administrator of Eastern Hai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again champion chief clerk to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang and prefect of Eastern Hai.

sentences.zh: 其年，會稽太守蔡興宗之郡，而惠開自京口請假還都，相逢於曲阿。

translations.literal: That year, when Cai Xingzong went out to his post as Administrator of Kuaiji, Huikai asked leave from Jingkou to return to the capital and met him at Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cai Xingzong departed for Kuaiji while Huikai, on leave from Jingkou, was returning to court; they met at Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 惠開先與興宗名位略同，又經情款，自以負釁摧屈，慮興宗不能詣己，戒勒部下：「蔡會稽部伍若借問，慎不得答。」

translations.literal: Huikai had earlier been nearly equal to Xingzong in name and rank and had once been on intimate terms; now, bearing guilt and crushed low, he feared Xingzong would not call on him and warned his followers: "If Cai of Kuaiji's party asks after Us, take care not to answer."
translations.idiomatic: They had once been peers and friendly; now, disgraced and humbled, he feared Xingzong would not visit him and ordered his men: "If anyone from Administrator Cai of Kuaiji inquires, do not answer."

sentences.zh: 惠開素嚴，自下莫敢違犯。

translations.literal: Huikai had always been severe; below him none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was famously stern; not one subordinate dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 興宗見惠開舟力甚盛，不知為誰，遣人歷舫訊，惠開有舫十餘，事力二三百人，皆低頭直去，無一人答者。

translations.literal: Xingzong saw Huikai's boats were very grand and did not know who it was; he sent men along the vessels to ask. Huikai had more than ten boats and two or three hundred attendants; all bowed their heads and went straight on—not one man replied.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong saw a mighty flotilla and sent men boat to boat to learn who it was. Huikai had more than ten craft and two or three hundred retainers; every man kept his head down and sailed on in silence.

sentences.zh: 復為晉平王休祐驃騎長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Champion Chief Clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, with the prefecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made champion chief clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, retaining the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，除少府，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Minister of the Privy Purse and given the additional title of Giver of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Minister of the Privy Purse with the added title Giver of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 惠開素剛，至是益不得志，寺內所住齋前，有向種花草甚美，惠開悉剗除，列種白揚樹。

translations.literal: Huikai had always been rigid; by now he was still more thwarted in his aims. Before the quarters where he dwelt in the temple he had planted flowering plants very beautiful; Huikai cut them all away and in rows planted white poplars.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had always been unyielding; now he was still more thwarted. In the garden before his monastic quarters stood fine flowering plants; he uprooted them all and planted rows of white poplars instead.

sentences.zh: 每謂人曰：「人生不得行胸懷，雖壽百歲，猶為夭也。」

translations.literal: He often told people: "If in life one cannot act out what is in one's breast, though one lives a hundred years it is still early death."
translations.idiomatic: He would say: "If a man cannot live out what is in his heart, a hundred years of life is still an early death."

sentences.zh: 發病歐血，吐如肝肺者甚多。

translations.literal: He fell ill and vomited blood; what he spat out like liver and lung was very much.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill, retched blood, and brought up masses that looked like liver and lung.

sentences.zh: 除巴陵王休若征西長史、寧朔將軍、南郡太守，未拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk to Prince Xiuruo of Baling, General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator of Nan commandery, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named chief clerk to Prince Xiuruo of Baling, General Who Pacifies the North, and prefect of Nan, but declined the posts.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子睿嗣，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Rui inherited; when Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui succeeded him; when the Qi dynasty took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 惠開與諸弟並不睦，惠基使益州，遂不相見。

translations.literal: Huikai was not on good terms with any of his younger brothers; when Huikai was sent to Yi province they never met again.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was estranged from all his brothers; once Huikai was posted to Yi, they never saw one another again.

sentences.zh: 與同產弟惠明亦著嫌隙云。

translations.literal: With his full brother Huiming he also had marked estrangement, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He was said to be at sharp odds even with his uterine brother Huiming.

sentences.zh: 殷琰，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Yan was a man of Changping in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan was a native of Changping in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 父道鸞，衡陽王義季右軍長史。

translations.literal: His father Dao Luan was Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Jiji of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao Luan had been Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Jiji of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 琰少為太祖所知，見遇與琅邪王景文相埒。

translations.literal: Yan in youth was known to the Founder; the favor shown him rivaled Prince Jingwen of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder noticed Yan in his youth and favored him almost as much as Prince Jingwen of Langye.

sentences.zh: 初為江夏王義恭征北行參軍，始興王濬後軍主簿，出為鄱陽、晉熙太守，豫州治中從事史，廬陵內史。

translations.literal: He first served as Pacifying-North Staff Officer under Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, Rear Army chief clerk under Prince Jun of Shixing, went out as Administrator of Poyang and Jinxī, Registrar of the Xu Inspectorate, and Interior Governor of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Pacifying-North staff officer to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, then rear-army chief clerk to Prince Jun of Shixing, then prefect of Poyang and Jinxī, Xu registrar, and interior governor of Luling.

sentences.zh: 臧質反，棄郡奔北皖。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi rebelled, he abandoned his commandery and fled to North Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rebelled, he abandoned his post and fled to North Wan.

sentences.zh: 琰性有計數，欲進退保全，故不還都邑。

translations.literal: Yan's nature was calculating; wishing to advance and retreat while preserving himself, he therefore did not return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was shrewd by nature and meant to keep his options open, so he did not go back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 事平，坐繫尚方，頃之被宥。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop; before long he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended he was held in the Imperial Workshop, then soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 除海陵王國郎中令，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Commandant of the Principality of Hailing but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered chief commandant of the Principality of Hailing but declined.

sentences.zh: 臨海王子頊為冠軍將軍、吳興太守，以琰為錄事參軍，行郡事。

translations.literal: When Prince Zixiang of Linhai was General Who Establishes the Army and Administrator of Wuxing, Yan was made Recorder and acted in the commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixiang of Linhai became General Who Establishes the Army and prefect of Wuxing, Yan served as recorder with acting charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 復為豫州別駕，太宰戶曹屬，丹陽丞，尚書左丞，少府，尋陽王子房冠軍司馬，行南豫州，隨府轉右軍司馬，又徙巴陵王休若左軍司馬。

translations.literal: He again served as Vice-Director of the Xu Inspectorate, staff member in the Grand Mentor's household bureau, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, Minister of the Privy Purse, Champion Staff Officer to Prince Zifang of Xunyang with acting charge of Southern Xu, then followed the prince as Right Army Staff Officer, and was moved to Left Army Staff Officer under Prince Xiuruo of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He was Xu vice-director, staff in the Grand Mentor's household office, Danyang assistant magistrate, Secretariat left assistant, privy purse minister, champion staff officer to Prince Zifang of Xunyang with acting Southern Xu, then right-army staff officer on the prince's staff, and finally left-army staff officer to Prince Xiuruo of Baling.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年，除黃門侍郎，出為山陽王休祐右軍長史、南梁郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongguang of the Deposed Emperor he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and went out as Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang and Administrator of Nanliang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongguang under the Deposed Emperor he became Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then right-army chief clerk to Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang and prefect of Nanliang.

sentences.zh: 休祐入朝，琰仍行府州事。

translations.literal: When Xiuyou entered court, Yan still acted in the prince's and province's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyou went to court, Yan continued to run the princely headquarters and the province.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始元年，以休祐為荊州，欲以吏部郎張岱為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi of Emperor Taizong, Xiuyou was given Jing province; the court wished to make Zhang Dai of the Ministry of Personnel Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's first year Xiuyou was shifted to Jing, and the court meant to appoint Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Zhang Dai inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 會晉安王子勛反，即以琰督豫、司二州、南豫州之梁郡諸軍事、建武將軍、豫州刺史，以西汝陰太守龐道隆為琰長史，殿中將軍劉順為司馬。

translations.literal: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled, Yan was at once made commander of the military affairs of Yu and Si provinces and Liang commandery of Southern Xu, General Who Establishes Martial Might, and Inspector of Yu; Pang Daolong, Administrator of Western Ruyin, was made Yan's Chief Clerk, and Palace Guard General Liu Shun his Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an rose, Yan was made commander of Yu and Si and of Liang in Southern Xu, General Who Establishes Martial Might, and Yu inspector; Pang Daolong of Western Ruyin became his chief clerk and Liu Shun of the palace guard his marshal.

sentences.zh: 順勸琰同子勛。

translations.literal: Shun urged Yan to join Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Shun pressed Yan to side with Zixun.

sentences.zh: 琰家累在京邑。

translations.literal: Yan's family dependents were all in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's whole family remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 意欲奉順，而土人前右軍參軍杜叔寶、前陳南頓二郡太守皇甫道烈、道烈從弟前馬頭太守景度、前汝南潁川二郡太守龐天生、前睢陽令夏侯季子等，並勸琰同逆。

translations.literal: He wished to follow Shun, but the local magnates—the former Right Army Staff Officer Du Shubao, the former Administrator of Chen and Nandun commanderies Huangfu Daolie, Daolie's cousin the former Administrator of Matou Jingdu, the former Administrator of Runan and Yingchuan Pang Tiansheng, and the former Magistrate of Suiyang Xiahou Jizi, among others—all urged Yan to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to obey Shun, but local strongmen—former staff officer Du Shubao, former prefect Huangfu Daolie of Chen and Nandun, Daolie's cousin former Matou prefect Jingdu, former Runan and Yingchuan prefect Pang Tiansheng, former Suiyang magistrate Xiahou Jizi, and others—all pushed him toward rebellion.

sentences.zh: 琰素無部曲，門義不過數人，無以自立，受制於叔寶等。

translations.literal: Yan had never had a personal guard; his household retainers numbered only a few men, and he could not stand on his own, but was controlled by Shubao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had no private troops and only a handful of household retainers; unable to stand alone, he fell under Shubao's control.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣冗從僕射柳倫領軍助，驃騎大將軍山陽王休祐又遣中兵參軍鄭瑗說琰令還。

translations.literal: Taizong sent the Supernumerary Attendant Liu Lun with an army to assist; the Grand General Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang also sent Staff Officer Zheng Yuan to persuade Yan to return.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Supernumerary Attendant Liu Lun with reinforcements, and Grand General Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang sent staff officer Zheng Yuan to call Yan back.

sentences.zh: 二人至，即與叔寶合。

translations.literal: When the two men arrived they at once joined Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Both men, on arrival, threw in with Shubao.

sentences.zh: 叔寶者，杜坦之子，既土豪鄉望，內外諸軍事並專之。

translations.literal: Shubao was the son of Du Tan; as local magnate and village elder he monopolized all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao, son of Du Tan, was the leading local magnate and kept every military matter in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 弋陽太守卜天生據郡同逆，斷梁州獻馬得百餘匹。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Yiyang, Bu Tiansheng, held his commandery in rebellion and cut off Liang province's tribute horses, obtaining more than a hundred head.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tiansheng, prefect of Yiyang, joined the revolt, seized over a hundred tribute horses bound for Liang province, and held the commandery.

sentences.zh: 邊城令宿僧護起義斬天生，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Biancheng, Su Sengdu, raised righteous troops, beheaded Tiansheng, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Su Sengdu, magistrate of Biancheng, rose in loyalist revolt, killed Tiansheng, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，以為龍驤將軍，封建興縣侯，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Taizong commended this and made him General of the Dragon Host, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jianxing with three hundred households' revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rewarded him with the title General of the Dragon Host and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jianxing with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時綏戎將軍、汝南、新蔡二郡太守周矜起義於懸瓠，收兵得千餘人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Jin, General Who Pacifies the Rong and Administrator of Runan and Xincai, raised troops at Xuanhu and gathered more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhou Jin, General Who Pacifies the Rong and prefect of Runan and Xincai, rebelled at Xuanhu and mustered over a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 袁顗遺信誘矜司馬汝南人常珍奇，以金鈴為信。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi sent a letter to entice Jin's Marshal Chang Zhenqi of Runan, using a gold bell as token.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi sent Chang Zhenqi, Jin's Runan marshal, a letter of enticement with a gold bell as pledge.

sentences.zh: 珍奇即日斬矜，送首詣顗，顗以珍奇為汝南、新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: Zhenqi that same day beheaded Jin, sent the head to Yi, and Yi made Zhenqi Administrator of Runan and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqi killed Jin the same day, sent his head to Yi, and Yi appointed Zhenqi prefect of Runan and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 太宗追贈矜本官，以義陽內史龐孟虯為司州刺史，領隨郡太守。

translations.literal: Taizong posthumously restored Jin's former office and made Pang Mengjiao, Interior Governor of Yiyang, Inspector of Si with concurrent charge of Suixiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong restored Jin's former rank posthumously and named Pang Mengjiao of Yiyang interior governor inspector of Si, with acting charge of Suixiang.

sentences.zh: 孟虯不受命，起兵同子勛。

translations.literal: Mengjiao did not accept the commission and raised troops to join Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjiao refused the order and took arms for Zixun.

sentences.zh: 子勛召孟虯出尋陽，而以孟虯子定光行義陽郡事。

translations.literal: Zixun summoned Mengjiao out to Xunyang and put Mengjiao's son Dingguang in charge of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun called Mengjiao to Xunyang and left his son Dingguang to govern Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗知琰逼迫土人，事不獲已，猶欲羈縻之。

translations.literal: Taizong knew Yan was forced by the local gentry and had not chosen this willingly, yet still wished to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew Yan was coerced by the locals and still hoped to win him back.

sentences.zh: 以琰兄前中書郎瑗為司徒右長史，子邈為山陽王休祐驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: He made Yan's elder brother, the former Gentleman at the Palace Secretariat Yuan, Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State, and Yan's son Miao a staff officer on Prince Xiuyou's Grand General council.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Yan's brother, former secretariat gentleman Yuan, to right chief clerk of the Minister of State, and Yan's son Miao to staff officer on Prince Xiuyou's council.

sentences.zh: 子勛遣使以琰為輔國將軍、梁郡太守，後又加豫州，假節督南豫數郡。

translations.literal: Zixun's envoy appointed Yan General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Liang commandery, and later added Yu province, with borrowed insignia to command several southern Xu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun's agents made Yan General Who Assists the State and Liang prefect, then added Yu province with acting insignia over several southern Xu districts.

sentences.zh: 杜叔寶求琰上佐，龐道隆慮其為禍，乃請奉表使尋陽。

translations.literal: Shubao asked Yan for a senior aide; Pang Daolong, fearing he would cause harm, requested leave to go to Xunyang with a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao demanded a senior aide; Daolong, fearing trouble, asked to carry a memorial to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 琰即以叔寶為長史、梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon made Shubao Chief Clerk and Administrator of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then made Shubao chief clerk and Liang prefect.

sentences.zh: 休祐步入朝，家內猶分停壽陽，琰資給供贍，事盡豐厚。

translations.literal: When Xiuyou entered court his household was still split and lodged at Shouyang; Yan supplied and supported them with the utmost generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou had gone to court while his family remained at Shouyang; Yan furnished them with lavish support.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，太宗遣輔國將軍劉勔率寧朔將軍呂安國西討，休祐出鎮歷陽，為諸軍總統。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, Taizong sent General Who Assists the State Liu Yan with General Who Pacifies the North Lü Anguo on a western campaign; Xiuyou went out to garrison Liyang as supreme commander of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, Taizong sent Liu Yan, General Who Assists the State, west with Lü Anguo, General Who Pacifies the North; Xiuyou took the field at Liyang as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都亦據彭城反，募能生禽琰、安都，封千戶縣侯，賜布絹各二千匹。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Andu, Inspector of Xu province, also held Pengcheng in rebellion; the court recruited anyone who could capture Yan or Andu alive with enfeoffment as Marquis of a thousand-household county and gifts of two thousand bolts of cloth and silk each.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, Xu inspector, also held Pengcheng in revolt; the throne promised a thousand-household marquisate and two thousand bolts of silk to whoever captured Yan or Andu alive.

sentences.zh: 二月，勔進軍小峴。

translations.literal: In the second month Yan advanced his army to Little Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Liu Yan marched to Little Xian.

sentences.zh: 初，合肥戍主、南汝陰太守薛元寶委郡奔子勛，前太守朱輔之據城歸順。

translations.literal: Earlier, the garrison commander of Hefei and Administrator of Southern Ruyin, Xue Yuanbao, had abandoned his commandery and fled to Zixun; the former Administrator Zhu Fuzhi held the city and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Hefei garrison chief and Southern Ruyin prefect Xue Yuanbao had earlier deserted to Zixun; former prefect Zhu Fuzhi held the city for the court.

sentences.zh: 琰遣攻輔之，輔之敗走。

translations.literal: Yan sent troops to attack Fuzhi; Fuzhi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yan attacked Fuzhi, who was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 琰以前右軍參軍裴季為南汝陰太守，季又歸順，太宗即而授之。

translations.literal: Yan appointed the former Right Army Staff Officer Pei Ji Administrator of Southern Ruyin; Ji again submitted, and Taizong confirmed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan named Pei Ji, a former right-army staff officer, Southern Ruyin prefect; when Ji defected, Taizong confirmed him.

sentences.zh: 琰所用象縣令許道蓮亦率二百人歸降，太宗以為馬頭太守。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xiang whom Yan had appointed, Xu Daolian, also led two hundred men in surrender; Taizong made him Administrator of Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daolian, Yan's magistrate of Xiang, also surrendered with two hundred men and was made Matou prefect.

sentences.zh: 三月，上又遣寧朔將軍劉懷珍、段僧愛、龍驤將軍姜產之馬步三軍，助勔討琰。

translations.literal: In the third month the court again sent General Who Pacifies the North Liu Huaizhen, Duan Song'ai, and General of the Dragon Host Jiang Chanzi with infantry and cavalry to assist Liu Yan in attacking Yin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court sent Liu Huaizhen and Duan Song'ai, Generals Who Pacify the North, and Jiang Chanzi, General of the Dragon Host, with horse and foot to reinforce Liu Yan against Yin Yan.

sentences.zh: 義軍主黃回募江西楚人千餘，斬子勛所置馬頭太守王廣元，以回為龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: The righteous-army leader Huang Hui recruited more than a thousand Chu men of western Jiang, beheaded Wang Guangyuan, whom Zixun had installed as Administrator of Matou, and was made General of the Dragon Host.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalist leader Huang Hui raised a thousand-odd western Jiang Chu fighters, killed Zixun's Matou prefect Wang Guangyuan, and was made General of the Dragon Host.

sentences.zh: 淮西人前奉朝請鄭墨率子弟部曲及淮右郡起義於陳郡城，有眾一萬，太宗以為司州刺史。

translations.literal: Zheng Mo of Huai west, former Court Gentleman for Submission, led kinsmen, retainers, and the commanderies of Huai right in uprising at Chen commandery city with ten thousand men; Taizong made him Inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: Former Court Gentleman Zheng Mo of western Huai led kin, retainers, and Huai-west commanderies in revolt at Chen city with ten thousand men and was named Si inspector.

sentences.zh: 後虜寇淮西，戰敗見殺，追贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later, when northern barbarians raided Huai west, he was defeated in battle and killed; posthumously he was given the rank General Who Establishes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed fighting northern raiders in Huai west and was posthumously made General Who Establishes the Army.

sentences.zh: 是月，劉順、柳倫、皇甫道烈、龐天生等馬步八千人，東據宛唐，去壽陽三百里。

translations.literal: That month Liu Shun, Liu Lun, Huangfu Daolie, Pang Tiansheng, and others with eight thousand horse and foot occupied Wanyang, three hundred li from Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shun, Lun, Daolie, Tiansheng, and others held Wanyang with eight thousand troops, three hundred li from Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 勔率眾軍並進，去順數里立營。

translations.literal: Liu Yan led the mass of armies forward together and encamped several li from Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan advanced with the main force and camped a few li from Shun.

sentences.zh: 在道遇雨，旦始至，壘塹未立，順欲擊之。

translations.literal: On the road they met rain; they arrived only at dawn, the ramparts and moats not yet finished, and Shun wished to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Rain slowed the march; they arrived at dawn with ditches unfinished, and Shun meant to strike at once.

sentences.zh: 時琰所遣諸軍並受節度，而以皇甫道烈、土豪柳倫，臺之所遣，順本卑微，不宜統督，唯二軍不受命。

translations.literal: All armies Yan had sent were under his command, but Huangfu Daolie and the local magnate Liu Lun had been sent by the court; Shun had originally been low in status and ought not to command overall—only those two armies did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's detachments were nominally under his orders, but Daolie and Lun answered to the court, and the low-born Shun was unfit for supreme command—only those two forces refused obedience.

sentences.zh: 至是道烈、倫不同，順不能獨進，乃止。

translations.literal: Now Daolie and Lun would not agree; Shun could not advance alone and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Daolie and Lun would not move; Shun could not attack alone and held back.

sentences.zh: 既而勔營壘漸立，不可復攻，因相持守。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Yan's ramparts were gradually completed and could not again be attacked; they therefore faced each other in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Yan's camp was fortified beyond assault, and the two sides settled into a standoff.

sentences.zh: 四月，勔錄事參軍王起、前部賊曹參軍甄澹等五人委勔奔順，順因此出軍攻勔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Liu Yan's Recorder Wang Qi, former Senior Clerk for Bandit Suppression Zhen Dan, and five others deserted Liu Yan for Shun; Shun therefore led his army out to attack Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Liu Yan's recorder Wang Qi and five others, including former bandit-suppression clerk Zhen Dan, defected to Shun, who then attacked Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 順幢主樊僧整與臺馬軍主驃騎中兵參軍段僧愛交矟鬥，僧整刺僧愛，殺之，追贈屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Shun's standard-bearer Fan Zhengzheng crossed spears with the court's cavalry commander, Grand General Staff Officer Duan Song'ai; Zhengzheng stabbed Song'ai and killed him; posthumously Song'ai was made Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's standard-bearer Fan Zhengzheng duelled court cavalry leader Duan Song'ai and killed him; Song'ai was posthumously made Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 僧愛勇冠三軍，軍中並懼。

translations.literal: Song'ai's valor led the three armies; within the army all feared.
translations.idiomatic: Song'ai had been the bravest man in the army, and his death shook the whole force.

sentences.zh: 太宗又遣太尉司馬垣閎率軍來會，步兵校尉龐沈之助裴季戍合肥。

translations.literal: Taizong also sent Grand Marshal Staff Officer Yuan Hong with troops to join up, and Infantry Commandant Pang Shenzhi to help Pei Ji garrison Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent staff officer Yuan Hong of the Grand Marshal's office with reinforcements and Infantry Commandant Pang Shenzhi to aid Pei Ji at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 初，淮南人周伯符說休祐求起義兵，休祐不許，固請，乃遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Bofu of Huainan had urged Xiuyou to raise righteous troops; Xiuyou did not permit it, but on his stubborn pleading sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhou Bofu of Huainan had begged Xiuyou for leave to raise loyalist troops; Xiuyou refused until Bofu pressed hard, then let him go.

sentences.zh: 杖策單行，至安豐，收得八百餘人，於淮西為遊兵。

translations.literal: Staff in hand he went alone to Anfeng, gathered more than eight hundred men, and on Huai west served as roving troops.
translations.idiomatic: He walked alone to Anfeng, collected eight hundred-odd men, and harried the Huai west as a roving band.

sentences.zh: 珍奇所置弋陽太守郭確遣將軍郭慈孫擊伯符於金丘，琰又遣中兵參軍杜叔寶助之。

translations.literal: Guo Que, whom Zhenqi had installed as Administrator of Yiyang, sent the general Guo Cisun to strike Bofu at Jinqiu; Yan also sent Staff Officer Du Shubao to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Que, Zhenqi's Yiyang prefect, sent Guo Cisun against Bofu at Jinqiu; Yan also sent Shubao to help.

sentences.zh: 慈孫等為伯符所敗，並投水死。

translations.literal: Cisun and the rest were defeated by Bofu and all threw themselves into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cisun was routed; he and his men drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 太宗以伯符為驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: Taizong made Bofu a staff officer on the Grand General's council.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made Bofu a grand-general staff officer.

sentences.zh: 叔寶本謂臺軍停住歷陽不辦進，順等至，無不瓦解，唯齎一月日糧。

translations.literal: Shubao had supposed the court army would halt at Liyang and not advance; when Shun and the rest arrived, everything would collapse—he brought only a month's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao had assumed the imperial army would stay at Liyang and that Shun's arrival would make everything collapse; he sent only a month's grain.

sentences.zh: 既與勔相持，軍食盡，報叔寶送食；

translations.literal: Once locked with Liu Yan in stalemate, army food was exhausted; he reported to Shubao to send food;
translations.idiomatic: Stalemated with Liu Yan, Shun's grain ran out and he begged Shubao for supplies;

sentences.zh: 叔寶乃發車千五百乘，載米餉順，自以五千精兵防送之。

translations.literal: Shubao then sent fifteen hundred carts loaded with rice to feed Shun, himself following with five thousand picked troops to escort it.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao dispatched fifteen hundred grain carts for Shun and escorted them with five thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 勔聞之，軍副呂安國曰：「劉順精甲八千，而我眾不能居半，相持既久，強弱勢殊，苟復推遷，則無以自立，所賴在彼糧將竭，我食有餘耳。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan heard this, his deputy Lü Anguo said: "Liu Shun has eight thousand elite armor, and our host is not half his strength. We have faced each other long; strong and weak are far apart. If we delay further we cannot stand. What we rely on is that their grain is nearly gone and ours still plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan heard this and his deputy Lü Anguo said: "Shun has eight thousand armored veterans and we are fewer than half his strength. The standoff has gone on too long; if we wait we cannot hold. Our hope is that their grain fails while ours still holds.

sentences.zh: 若使叔寶米至，非唯難可復圖，我亦不能持久。

translations.literal: If Shubao's rice arrives, not only will it be hard to achieve our plan again, we also cannot endure long.
translations.idiomatic: If Shubao's grain gets through, we can neither win nor last.

sentences.zh: 今唯有間道襲其米車，出彼不意。

translations.literal: Now we have only to take a bypath and strike his grain carts, catching him unawares.
translations.idiomatic: We must take a hidden road and strike the convoy by surprise.

sentences.zh: 若能制之，將不戰走矣。」

translations.literal: If we can seize it, the army will flee without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Seize the grain and they will run without a battle."

sentences.zh: 勔以為然，乃以疲弱守營，簡選千百精手，配安國及軍主黃回等，間路出順後，於橫塘抄之。

translations.literal: Liu Yan agreed and left the weak to hold camp, chose a thousand-odd picked men, paired Anguo with the army leader Huang Hui, and by a hidden road went out behind Shun to strike at Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan agreed, left weak troops in camp, picked a thousand veterans under Anguo and Huang Hui, and stole behind Shun to ambush the convoy at Hengtang.

sentences.zh: 安國始行，計叔寶尋至，止齎二日熟食，食盡，叔寶不至，將士並欲還。

translations.literal: When Anguo set out he calculated Shubao would soon arrive and carried only two days' cooked food; when the food was gone and Shubao had not come, the officers and men all wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo reckoned Shubao was near and carried only two days' rations; when these were gone and Shubao still absent, his men wanted to turn back.

sentences.zh: 安國曰：「卿等旦已一食，今晚米車不容不至。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "You have already eaten once today; tonight the grain carts cannot fail to come.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said: "You have eaten once today; tonight the carts must come.

sentences.zh: 若其不至，夜去不晚。」

translations.literal: If they do not come, it will not be too late to leave by night."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not, we can withdraw after dark."

sentences.zh: 叔寶果至，以米車為函箱陣，叔寶於外為遊軍，幢主楊仲懷領五百人居前，與安國、回等相會。

translations.literal: Shubao indeed came; he formed the rice carts into a box-cart formation, with himself as roving army outside; the standard-bearer Yang Zhonghuai led five hundred men in front and met Anguo, Hui, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao came, drew the carts into a box formation, screened them with a flying column, and sent Yang Zhonghuai with five hundred men ahead to meet Anguo and Hui.

sentences.zh: 仲懷部曲並欲退就叔寶，并力擊安國。

translations.literal: Zhonghuai's troops all wished to fall back toward Shubao and combine strength to strike Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghuai's men wanted to fall back on Shubao and hit Anguo together.

sentences.zh: 仲懷曰：「賊至不擊，復欲何待？

translations.literal: Zhonghuai said: "The bandits have come—will you not strike? What are you waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghuai said: "The enemy is here—why hold back? What are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 且統軍在後，政三二里間，比吾交手，何憂不至。」

translations.literal: Moreover the commander-in-chief is behind, only two or three li away; by the time we join hands, why worry he will not arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: The main army is two or three li behind; once we engage, they will come."

sentences.zh: 即便前戰，回所領並淮南楚子，天下精兵，眾力既倍，合戰，便破之。

translations.literal: He at once advanced to battle; those under Hui were all Chu men of Huainan, the finest troops under heaven; their combined strength was doubled; in the engagement they at once broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He charged; Hui's Huainan Chu were the finest fighters in the empire, and at double strength they shattered the van at once.

sentences.zh: 於陣殺仲懷，仲懷所領五百人死盡。

translations.literal: In the formation Zhonghuai was killed; the five hundred under Zhonghuai all died to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghuai fell in the fight and all five hundred of his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 叔寶至，而仲懷及士卒伏屍蔽野，回等欲乘勝擊之，安國曰：「彼將自走，不假復擊。」

translations.literal: When Shubao arrived, Zhonghuai and the soldiers lay dead covering the field; Hui and the rest wished to press the victory and strike, but Anguo said: "They will flee on their own—no need to strike again."
translations.idiomatic: Shubao arrived to find the field heaped with dead; Hui wanted to press the attack, but Anguo said: "They will run on their own—no need to strike again.

sentences.zh: 退軍三十里止宿，夜遣騎參候，叔寶果棄米車奔走。

translations.literal: They withdrew the army thirty li and halted for the night; at night they sent horsemen to reconnoiter; Shubao indeed abandoned the grain carts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew thirty li and camped; night scouts found Shubao had abandoned the carts and fled.

sentences.zh: 安國即復夜往，燒米車，驅牛二千餘頭而還。

translations.literal: Anguo at once went again by night, burned the grain carts, and drove back more than two thousand head of cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo returned by night, burned the carts, and drove off more than two thousand cattle.

sentences.zh: 劉順聞米車見燒，叔寶又走，五月一日夜，眾潰，奔還壽陽，仍走淮西就常珍奇。

translations.literal: When Liu Shun heard the grain carts were burned and Shubao had also fled, on the night of the first day of the fifth month the host collapsed, fled back to Shouyang, and still went to Huai west to join Chang Zhenqi.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the convoy was burned and Shubao fled, Shun's army collapsed on the night of the first of the fifth month; they fled to Shouyang and then west to join Chang Zhenqi.

sentences.zh: 勔於是方軌而進。

translations.literal: Liu Yan then advanced in ordered columns.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan then marched in full array on Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 叔寶斂居民及散卒，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Shubao gathered the residents and scattered soldiers and clung to the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao rallied townsfolk and broken troops and shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 勔與諸軍分營城外，黃回立航渡肥水。

translations.literal: Liu Yan and the armies divided camps outside the walls; Huang Hui built a pontoon to cross the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan ringed the city with camps while Huang Hui threw a pontoon bridge across the Fei.

sentences.zh: 叔寶遣馬步三千，欲破航，並柵斷小峴埭，回擊大破之，焚其船柵。

translations.literal: Shubao sent three thousand horse and foot to break the bridge and also palisaded the Little Xian dam; Hui counterattacked and broke them severely, burning their boats and palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao sent three thousand men to destroy the bridge and bar the Little Xian sluice; Hui routed them and burned their boats and palisades.

sentences.zh: 休祐與琰書曰：「君本文弱，素無武幹，是遠近所悉，且名器清顯，不應復有分外希覬。

translations.literal: Xiuyou wrote to Yan: "You, sir, were by nature literarily weak and never had military talent—this is what near and far all know. Moreover your name and office are pure and eminent; you ought not again to have extravagant hopes beyond your station.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou wrote to Yan: "You have always been known as a man of letters, not a soldier, and your rank is already high; you should not harbor further ambition.

sentences.zh: 近者之事，當是劫於凶豎，不能守節。

translations.literal: Your recent conduct must be that you were coerced by vicious fellows and could not keep your integrity.
translations.idiomatic: What you have done lately was surely forced on you by ruffians—you could not keep your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今大軍長驅，已造城下，勢孤援絕，禍敗交至，顧昔情款，猶有惻然。

translations.literal: Now the great army drives far; it has already reached below the walls. Your strength is isolated, aid cut off; disaster and defeat come together. Looking back on our old affection, I still feel compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial host is at the walls; you are alone and cut off, ruin upon you—and yet, remembering old friendship, I am still moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 聖上垂天地之仁，開不世之澤，好生惡殺，遐邇所聞。

translations.literal: The Sage Emperor extends the benevolence of heaven and earth, opens grace without parallel in the age, loves life and hates killing—far and near have heard it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mercy spans heaven and earth; his grace is unmatched; he loves life and abhors slaughter—the whole realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 顧琛、王曇生等皆軍敗迸走，披草乞活，尚蒙恩恕，晏處私門。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, and others all were defeated in battle and fled headlong, parted the grass to beg for life, and still received imperial pardon, dwelling at ease in their private gates.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, and others fled defeated, crawled through the grass to beg their lives, and were pardoned to live quietly at home.

sentences.zh: 今神鋒所臨，前無橫陳，況窮城弱眾，殘傷之餘，而欲自固乎！

translations.literal: Now where the divine blades look down, nothing stands athwart before them—how much less a beleaguered city with a weak host, the remnant of the wounded, yet wishing to hold firm!
translations.idiomatic: Where the imperial blades point, nothing blocks their path—will a broken garrison in a doomed city still try to hold out?

sentences.zh: 若開門歸順，自可不失富貴；

translations.literal: If you open the gates and submit, you may naturally keep wealth and honor;
translations.idiomatic: Open the gates and submit, and you may keep your wealth and rank;

sentences.zh: 將佐小大，並保榮爵。

translations.literal: officers great and small will all preserve their noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and every officer, high or low, will keep his honors.

sentences.zh: 何故苟困士民，自求齏膾，身膏斧鑊，妻息並盡，老兄垂白，東市受刑邪！

translations.literal: Why stubbornly distress officers and people, seek minced meat for yourself, smear your body on the axe and cauldron, wife and children all destroyed, your elder brother white-haired, receiving punishment at the eastern market!
translations.idiomatic: Why torment soldiers and civilians, court the chopping block, doom your wife and children, and send your white-haired elder brother to die at the eastern market!

sentences.zh: 幸自思之。

translations.literal: I beg you to think on it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Think on this yourself.

sentences.zh: 信言不爽，有如皎日。」

translations.literal: These sincere words will not fail, bright as the noonday sun."
translations.idiomatic: My word stands as clear as the noon sun."

sentences.zh: 上又遣王道隆齎詔宥琰罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent Wang Daolong bearing an edict to pardon Yan's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Wang Daolong with an edict pardoning Yan's offenses.

sentences.zh: 勔又與琰書曰：「昔景和凶悖，行絕人倫，昏虐險穢，諫諍杜塞，遂殘毀陵廟，芟刈百僚，縱毒窮凶，靡有紀極。

translations.literal: Liu Yan also wrote to Yan: "Formerly Emperor Jinghe was fierce and perverse, his conduct cutting off human relations, benighted, cruel, treacherous, and foul; remonstrance was blocked; he then mutilated the imperial tombs and temples, mowed down the hundred officials, unleashed poison to the limit of villainy, without any boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan also wrote to Yan: "Emperor Jinghe was savage and unnatural, cruel and depraved; he silenced all counsel, desecrated the ancestral temples, slaughtered the bureaucracy, and indulged evil without limit.

sentences.zh: 于時人神回遑，莫能自保，中外士庶，咸願一匡。

translations.literal: At that time men and spirits alike were distraught and could not preserve themselves; within and without, gentlemen and commoners all wished for one restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Men and gods alike were in turmoil; court and country longed for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 予職在直衛，目所備睹。

translations.literal: My duty lay in the direct guard; my eyes were fully witness.
translations.idiomatic: I served in the palace guard and saw it all with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 主上神機天發，指麾克定，橫流塗炭，一朝太平，扶危拯急，實冠終古。

translations.literal: Our lord's divine strategy issued from heaven; at his command all was settled; the flood across the land turned to charcoal—in one morning peace came; supporting the endangered and rescuing the urgent truly crowns all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord's genius answered heaven; with a gesture he stilled the flood of blood and ash and restored peace in a day—such rescue of a tottering realm has no parallel in history.

sentences.zh: 而四方持疑，成此乖逆，資斧所臨，每從偃簡。

translations.literal: Yet the four quarters held doubts and produced this perverse revolt; where the imperial axe looked down, each time it was stayed and eased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the provinces hesitated and rebellion spread; wherever the imperial armies marched, mercy followed.

sentences.zh: 足下以衣冠華胄，信槩夙昭，附戾從違，猶見容養。

translations.literal: You, sir, as a cap-and-gown noble scion whose integrity has long been manifest—even in joining perversity and following rebellion—are still shown forbearance and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: You are a gentleman of eminent house and long-proven honor; even in siding with rebellion you have been treated with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 賢兄長史，階升清列；

translations.literal: Your worthy elder brother the Chief Clerk has risen step by step into the pure ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Your brother the chief clerk has been promoted into the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 賢子參軍，亦塞國網。

translations.literal: your worthy son the staff officer also fills the state's net of office.
translations.idiomatic: your son the staff officer also holds a post in the imperial service.

sentences.zh: 間者進軍宛唐，計由劉順，退眾閉城，當時未了。

translations.literal: Recently in advancing on Wanyang the plan came from Liu Shun; the army withdrew and shut the city—the matter was then unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: The recent move on Wanyang was Shun's doing; the force withdrew and shut the gates, and the affair was left unsettled.

sentences.zh: 過蒙朝恩，謬充將帥，蚤承風素，情有依然。

translations.literal: Overreceiving the court's grace, I was wrongly placed as commander; long ago I received your manner and style, and feeling remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: I have been undeservedly honored as commander, yet I have known you long and my regard is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 今皇威遠申，三方蹙弱，勝敗之勢，皎然可覽。

translations.literal: Now imperial majesty extends far; the three directions are pressed and weak; the trend of victory and defeat is bright and can be surveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial might now fills the realm; the rebel zones shrink; who will win is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 王御史昨至，主上敕、驃騎教、賢兄賢子書，今悉遣送。

translations.literal: Censor Wang arrived yesterday; the Emperor's command, the Grand General's instruction, and letters to your worthy brother and worthy son are all now sent along.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Wang has arrived with the emperor's decree, the grand general's order, and letters to your brother and son—all enclosed.

sentences.zh: 百代以來，未有弘恩曲宥，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Through a hundred generations there has never been such vast grace and bent pardon reaching to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: In a hundred generations there has never been mercy so broad.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷方宣示大義，惟新王道，何容摽虛辭於士女，失國信於一州。

translations.literal: Moreover the court is now proclaiming the great principle and renewing the kingly way—how could it bear to post empty words to gentlemen and ladies and lose the state's trust in one province?
translations.idiomatic: The court is proclaiming a new order; how can you parade false promises to your people and forfeit the empire's trust in a whole province?

sentences.zh: 以足下明識淵見，想必不俟終日。

translations.literal: With your bright knowledge and deep insight, I believe you surely will not wait until the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: A man of your insight will surely not wait until the last hour.

sentences.zh: 如其孤背亭毒，弗忌屠陷者，便當窮兵肆武，究法極刑。

translations.literal: If you alone turn your back on tender care and do not fear slaughter and ruin, then we shall exhaust arms and unleash force, carrying law to the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: If you stubbornly reject this mercy and do not fear annihilation, we shall unleash the full force of arms and the utmost penalties of law.

sentences.zh: 將恐貴門無復祭祀之主，墳壟乏掃灑之望。

translations.literal: I fear your noble house will have no one left to lead the sacrifices, and the tombs will lack the hope of sweeping and tending.
translations.idiomatic: Your clan may lack heirs to tend the ancestral rites, your graves none to sweep.

sentences.zh: 進謝忠臣，退慚孝子，名實兩喪，沒有餘責。

translations.literal: Advancing, you fail the loyal minister; retreating, you shame the filial son; name and reality both lost, with nothing left to answer for.
translations.idiomatic: You will fail as a loyal servant and shame yourself as a filial son; fame and duty alike destroyed, you will have nothing left.

sentences.zh: 扶力略白，幸加研覽。」

translations.literal: Fu Li briefly states this; I beg you to study and peruse it."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Li offers this brief word and asks you to consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 琰本無反心，事由力屈，叔寶等有降意，前後屢遣送誠箋，而眾心持疑，莫能相一，故歸順之計，每多愆塞，嬰城愈固。

translations.literal: Yan originally had no heart to rebel; the matter arose from being forced by power. Shubao and others had intent to surrender and repeatedly sent letters of sincerity, but the common will held doubts and could not unite; therefore plans to submit were often obstructed, and clinging to the city grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had never meant to rebel but was overpowered; Shubao and others wished to surrender and sent repeated pledges of loyalty, yet the garrison could not agree, so every plan to submit failed and the defense only hardened.

sentences.zh: 弋陽西山蠻田益之起義，攻郭確於弋陽，以益之為輔國將軍，督弋陽西山事。

translations.literal: Tian Yizhi, a Man of western Yiyang, raised righteous troops, attacked Guo Que at Yiyang, and was made General Who Assists the State with command over western Yiyang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizhi, a tribal leader of western Yiyang, rebelled against Guo Que and was made General Who Assists the State with charge of western Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，勔築長圍始合。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Liu Yan's long encirclement was first closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Yan completed the long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 田益之率蠻眾萬餘人攻龐定光於義陽，定光遣從兄文生拒之，為益之所破，見殺，遂圍其城。

translations.literal: Tian Yizhi led more than ten thousand Man troops to attack Pang Dingguang at Yiyang; Dingguang sent his cousin Wensheng to resist; he was broken by Yizhi and killed, and they then besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizhi led ten thousand-odd tribesmen against Pang Dingguang at Yiyang; Dingguang's cousin Wensheng resisted, was defeated and killed, and Yizhi besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 定光求救於子勛，子勛以定光父孟虯為司州刺史，率精兵五千救義陽，并解壽陽之圍。

translations.literal: Dingguang begged rescue from Zixun; Zixun made Dingguang's father Mengjiao Inspector of Si, led five thousand elite troops to save Yiyang, and also lift the siege of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguang called on Zixun, who made his father Mengjiao Si inspector and sent five thousand elite troops to relieve Yiyang and break the siege of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 常珍奇又自懸瓠遣三千人援定光，屯軍柳水。

translations.literal: Chang Zhenqi also from Xuanhu sent three thousand men to aid Dingguang, encamping at Liushui.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhenqi sent three thousand men from Xuanhu to reinforce Dingguang at Liushui.

sentences.zh: 益之不戰，望風奔散。

translations.literal: Yizhi did not fight and scattered at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 孟虯乘勝進軍向壽陽。

translations.literal: Mengjiao pressed his victory and advanced the army toward Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjiao marched on Shouyang in triumph.

sentences.zh: 初，常珍奇遣周當、垣式寶率數百人送仗與琰。
