translations.literal: Earlier, Chang Zhenqi sent Zhou Dang and Yuan Shibao with several hundred men to deliver weapons to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chang Zhenqi had sent Zhou Dang and Yuan Shibao with several hundred men to bring arms to Yan.

sentences.zh: 式寶驍勇絕眾，因留守北門，乃率所領，開門掩襲勔，入其營；

translations.literal: Shibao's daring valor surpassed the host; as he was left to hold the north gate, he led those under him, opened the gate, and made a surprise strike on Liu Yan, entering his camp;
translations.idiomatic: Shibao was exceptionally bold; left to hold the north gate, he sallied out, surprised Liu Yan's camp, and broke in;

sentences.zh: 勔逃避得免，式寶得勔衣帽而去。

translations.literal: Liu Yan fled and escaped; Shibao took Liu Yan's hat and robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan escaped; Shibao seized his hat and cloak and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勔於是乃豎長圍，治攻道於東南角，並填塹。

translations.literal: Liu Yan then raised the long encirclement, prepared assault routes at the southeast corner, and also filled the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan then tightened the siege, opened assault lanes at the southeast corner, and began filling the moat.

sentences.zh: 東南角有高樓，隊主趙法進計曰：「外若進攻，必先攻樓，樓頹落，既傷將士，又使人情沮壞，不如先自毀之。」

translations.literal: At the southeast corner was a high tower; the squad leader Zhao Fujin advised: "If the outside attacks, they will surely attack the tower first; when the tower collapses it will both wound officers and soldiers and break men's spirits—better to destroy it ourselves first."
translations.idiomatic: A tall tower stood at the southeast corner; squad leader Zhao Fujin said: "The attackers will strike the tower first; when it falls it will kill our men and break morale—better destroy it ourselves.

sentences.zh: 從其言。

translations.literal: They followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: They did so.

sentences.zh: 勔用草茅苞土，擲以塞塹。

translations.literal: Liu Yan used straw wrapped around clods of earth and threw them to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan hurled bundles of straw-wrapped earth into the moat.

sentences.zh: 擲者如雲，城內乃以火箭射之，草未及燃，後土續至，一二日，塹便欲滿。

translations.literal: The throwers were like clouds; within the city they shot fire arrows at them; the straw had not yet burned when earth followed after; in a day or two the moat was nearly full.
translations.idiomatic: The bundles flew like clouds; the defenders shot fire arrows, but before the straw caught, fresh earth kept coming; within two days the moat was nearly filled.

sentences.zh: 趙法進復獻計，以鐵珠子灌之。

translations.literal: Zhao Fujin again offered a plan: pour iron beads down on them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fujin proposed pouring iron pellets onto the bundles.

sentences.zh: 珠子流滑，悉緣隙得入，草於是火燃，二日間草盡，塹中土不過二三寸。

translations.literal: The beads flowed slickly and all entered through the gaps; the straw then caught fire; within two days the straw was gone and the earth in the moat was no more than two or three inches.
translations.idiomatic: The beads slipped through every gap; the straw ignited and burned away in two days, leaving only two or three inches of earth in the moat.

sentences.zh: 勔乃作大蝦蟆車載土，牛皮蒙之，三百人推以塞塹。

translations.literal: Liu Yan then made great toad carts carrying earth, covered with oxhide; three hundred men pushed them to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan built great "toad carts" laden with earth, covered in oxhide, and pushed by three hundred men to fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 琰戶曹參軍虞挹之造碻車，擊之以石，車悉破壞。

translations.literal: Yan's Household Bureau Staff Officer Yu Yizhi built catapult carts and struck them with stones; the carts were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's household officer Yu Yizhi built stone-throwing engines and smashed every cart.

sentences.zh: 初，廬江太守王子仲棄郡奔尋陽，廬江人起義，休祐遣員外散騎侍郎陸悠之助之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Administrator of Lujiang, Wang Zizhong, abandoned his commandery and fled to Xunyang; the people of Lujiang rose in revolt, and Xiuyou sent Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Lu Youzhi to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lujiang prefect Wang Zizhong had deserted to Xunyang; the people of Lujiang rebelled, and Xiuyou sent secretariat gentleman Lu Youzhi to help them.

sentences.zh: 劉胡遣其輔國將軍薛道摽渡江煽動群蠻，規自廬江掩襲歷陽，悠之眾弱，退保譙城。

translations.literal: Liu Hu sent his General Who Assists the State Xue Daobiao across the river to stir the Man tribes, planning from Lujiang to strike Liyang by surprise; Youzhi's host was weak and retreated to hold Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent Xue Daobiao, General Who Assists the State, across the Yangzi to rouse the tribes and strike Liyang from Lujiang; Youzhi, outnumbered, fell back to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王休仁遣參軍沈靈寵馳據廬江，道摽後一日方至，悠之自譙城來會，因與道摽相持。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, Minister of State, sent Staff Officer Shen Lingchong to seize Lujiang at speed; Daobiao arrived one day later; Youzhi came from Qiao city to join him, and thus they faced Daobiao in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an sent Shen Lingchong to seize Lujiang; Daobiao arrived a day late; Youzhi marched from Qiao to join Shen, and the two held Daobiao at bay.

sentences.zh: 七月，龐孟虯至弋陽，勔遣呂安國、垣閎、龍驤將軍陳顯達、驃騎參軍孟次陽拒之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Pang Mengjiao reached Yiyang; Liu Yan sent Lü Anguo, Yuan Hong, General of the Dragon Host Chen Xianda, and Grand General Staff Officer Meng Ciyang to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Mengjiao reached Yiyang; Liu Yan sent Lü Anguo, Yuan Hong, Chen Xianda, and Meng Ciyang against him.

sentences.zh: 孟虯軍副呂興壽與安國有舊，率所領降。

translations.literal: Mengjiao's army deputy Lü Xingshou was old friends with Anguo and led those under him in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjiao's deputy Lü Xingshou, an old friend of Anguo's, surrendered with his command.

sentences.zh: 安國進軍，破孟虯於蓼潭，義軍主陳肫又破之於汝水，孟虯走向義陽；

translations.literal: Anguo advanced and broke Mengjiao at Liaotan; the righteous-army leader Chen Tun again broke him at the Ru River; Mengjiao fled toward Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Anguo routed Mengjiao at Liaotan; loyalist leader Chen Tun beat him again on the Ru; Mengjiao fled toward Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 義陽已為王玄謨子曇善起義所據，乃逃於蠻中。

translations.literal: Yiyang had already been seized by Wang Xuamo's son Tanshan, who raised righteous troops, and he therefore fled into the Man lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang was already held by Wang Xuamo's son Tanshan, who had risen in revolt, so Mengjiao fled among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 淮西人鄭叔舉起義擊常珍奇，以為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Zheng Shuju of Huai west raised righteous troops to strike Chang Zhenqi and was made Inspector of Northern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shuju of western Huai rebelled against Chang Zhenqi and was made Northern Yu inspector.

sentences.zh: 八月，皇甫道烈、柳倫等二十一人聞孟虯敗，並開門出降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Huangfu Daolie, Liu Lun, and twenty-one others, hearing of Mengjiao's defeat, all opened their gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Daolie, Lun, and twenty-one others, hearing of Mengjiao's defeat, opened their gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 勔因此又與琰書曰：「柳倫來奔，具相申述，方承足下跡纏穢亂，心秉忠誠，惘默窮愁，不親戎政。

translations.literal: Liu Yan therefore again wrote to Yan: "Liu Lun came over in flight and fully reported in detail; I now receive that your footsteps are entangled in foul rebellion, yet your heart holds loyalty and sincerity—you are silent in distress and do not personally attend to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan wrote again: "Lun has defected and told me everything. I understand you are caught in rebellion against your will, loyal at heart but silent and withdrawn from command.

sentences.zh: 去冬開天之始，愚迷者多，如足下流比，進非社稷宗臣，退無顧命寄託，朝廷既不偏相嫌責，足下亦復無所獨愧。

translations.literal: At the opening of heaven last winter, the deluded were many; men of your sort are neither advancing as ministers of the altars of state nor retreating with a dying sovereign's charge—the court does not on one side blame and suspect, and you likewise have nothing to be uniquely ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: When the new reign began last winter many were confused; men like you were neither great ministers of state nor bearers of a deathbed charge—the court does not single you out for blame, and you need not bear unique guilt.

sentences.zh: 程天祚已舉城歸順，龐孟虯又繼跡奔亡，劉胡困於錢溪，袁顗欲戰不得，推理揆勢，亦安能久。

translations.literal: Cheng Tianzuo has already raised his city in submission; Pang Mengjiao has again followed in flight; Liu Hu is trapped at Qianxi; Yuan Yi wishes to fight but cannot—reasoning out and measuring the trend, how can it last long?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tianzuo has surrendered his city; Mengjiao is in flight; Liu Hu is trapped at Qianxi; Yuan Yi cannot give battle—judge the trend and see it cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 且南方初起，連州十六，擁徒百萬，仲春以來，無戰不北，摧陷殄滅，十無一二。

translations.literal: Moreover the south at first rose with sixteen contiguous provinces and a million followers; since mid-spring there has been no battle that did not go north in defeat—broken, crushed, and extinguished—not one or two in ten remain.
translations.idiomatic: The southern revolt began with sixteen provinces and a million men; since mid-spring every battle has been lost; nine in ten are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 南憑袁顗弱卒，北恃足下孤城，以茲定業，恐萬無一理。

translations.literal: In the south relying on Yuan Yi's weak soldiers, in the north depending on your lone city—to settle the enterprise on this, I fear there is not one chance in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuan Yi's feeble force in the south and your lone city in the north, to build an empire on that has not one chance in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 方今國網疏略，示舉宏維，比日相白，想亦已具矣。

translations.literal: Now the state's net is broad and loose, displaying the great sustaining cords; what was told you these recent days, I think, is already complete.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is being reordered on a grand scale; you have already heard the full report in recent days.

sentences.zh: 且倫等皆是足下腹心牙爪，所以攜手相捨，非有怨恨也，了知事不可濟，禍害已及故耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Lun and the rest are all your belly-heart, teeth, and claws; the reason they joined hands in leaving you is not that they bore resentment—they clearly knew the affair could not succeed and disaster had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and the others were your closest lieutenants; they left not from spite but because they saw the cause was doomed and ruin at hand.

sentences.zh: 夫擁數千烏合，抗天下之兵，傾覆之狀，豈不易曉。

translations.literal: To hold several thousand gathered rabble and resist the armies of all under heaven—the shape of overturning is surely not hard to discern.
translations.idiomatic: A few thousand rabble against the armies of the empire—how collapse looks is not hard to see.

sentences.zh: 假令六蔽之人，猶當不為其事，況復足下少祖名教，疾沒世無稱者邪。

translations.literal: Even if one were a man blind in all six directions, he should still not do this thing—how much less you, sir, who in youth honor name and teaching and hate to leave the world without praise!
translations.idiomatic: Even a blind fool would refuse this course—how much less a man bred on the classics who dreads leaving no name behind!

sentences.zh: 所以復有此白者，實惜華州重鎮，鞠為茂草，兼傷貴門一日屠滅。

translations.literal: The reason I again have this statement is that I truly pity this heavy stronghold of Huazhou, reduced to rank grass, and grieve that your noble house may in one day be slaughtered to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: I write again because I pity this great fortress of Huazhou turning to wasteland and your noble house wiped out in a day.

sentences.zh: 足下若能封府庫，開四門，宣語文武，示以禍福，先遣咫尺之書，表達誠款，然後素車白馬，來詣轅門，若令足下髮膚不全，兒姪彫耗者，皇天后土，實聞此言。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can seal the treasuries, open the four gates, proclaim to civil and military, show fortune and disaster, first send a letter within a foot's measure expressing sincere intent, then come in plain cart and white horse to the camp gate—if I cause your hair and skin to be incomplete or your sons and nephews to be cut down and wasted, may High Heaven and Earthly Sovereign truly hear these words.
translations.idiomatic: Seal the treasuries, open the gates, tell your officers the choice before them, send a letter of submission, then come in the white cart of surrender—if I harm a hair on your head or one of your kin, let heaven and earth witness my oath.

sentences.zh: 至辭不華，寧復多白。」

translations.literal: Coming to words without ornament, why speak more?"
translations.idiomatic: I will not embellish further."

sentences.zh: 薛道摽猶在廬江，劉胡又分兵揚聲向壽陽及合肥。

translations.literal: Xue Daobiao was still in Lujiang; Liu Hu also divided troops to proclaim movement toward Shouyang and Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Daobiao still held Lujiang while Liu Hu feigned marches on Shouyang and Hefei.

sentences.zh: 勔遣許道蓮馳赴合肥，助裴季文，又遣黃回、孟次陽乃屯騎校尉段佛榮、武衛將軍王廣之繼之。

translations.literal: Liu Yan sent Xu Daolian at speed to Hefei to aid Pei Jiwen, and also sent Huang Hui, Meng Ciyang, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Duan Furong, and General of the Martial Guard Wang Guangzhi after them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan rushed Xu Daolian to aid Pei Jiwen at Hefei, then sent Huang Hui, Meng Ciyang, Duan Furong, and Wang Guangzhi in support.

sentences.zh: 道摽率其黨薛元寶等攻合肥，勔所遣諸軍未至，為道摽所陷，季文及武衛將軍葉慶祖力戰死之。

translations.literal: Daobiao led his faction Xue Yuanbao and others to attack Hefei; the armies Liu Yan had sent had not yet arrived and were taken by Daobiao; Jiwen and General of the Martial Guard Ye Qingzu fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: Daobiao attacked Hefei with Yuanbao before Liu Yan's reinforcements arrived; Jiwen and Ye Qingzu were killed in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 勔馳遣垣閎總統諸軍攻合肥。

translations.literal: Liu Yan urgently sent Yuan Hong to command overall the armies attacking Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan hurried Yuan Hong to take overall command at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 是月，劉胡敗走，尋陽平定。

translations.literal: That month Liu Hu was defeated and fled; Xunyang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Hu was routed and Xunyang fell.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣叔寶從父弟季文至琰城下，與叔寶語，說四方已定，勸令時降。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Shubao's cousin Jiwen to below Yan's walls to speak with Shubao, telling him the four quarters were already settled and urging timely surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Shubao's cousin Jiwen to parley under the walls, saying the realm was pacified and urging surrender.

sentences.zh: 叔寶曰：「我乃信汝，恐為人所誑耳！」

translations.literal: Shubao said: "I could trust you—but I fear being deceived by others!"
translations.idiomatic: Shubao said: "I might trust you, but I fear others are deceiving me!"

sentences.zh: 叔寶閉絕子勛敗問，有傳者即殺之。

translations.literal: Shubao cut off all news of Zixun's defeat; whoever spread word of it was at once killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao suppressed all news of Zixun's defeat and killed anyone who spread it.

sentences.zh: 時琰子邈東在京邑，繫建康，太宗送邈與琰，令說南賊已平之問，自建康出，便防送就道。

translations.literal: At that time Yan's son Miao was in the eastern capital, held at Jiankang; Taizong sent Miao to Yan to tell him the southern rebels were already pacified; from the time he left Jiankang he was escorted under guard on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Miao was held at Jiankang; Taizong sent him to his father with word that the south was pacified, under guard from the moment he left the capital.

sentences.zh: 議者以為宜聽邈與伯父瑗私相見，不爾無以解城內之惑，不從。

translations.literal: Advisers thought Miao ought to be allowed a private meeting with his uncle Yuan, otherwise there would be no way to dispel doubt within the city; this was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel held that Miao should be allowed to meet his uncle Yuan privately to clear the garrison's doubts; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 邈至，叔寶等果疑，守備方固。

translations.literal: When Miao arrived, Shubao and the rest indeed grew suspicious, and the defense grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao arrived, Shubao and the rest only grew more suspicious and tightened the defense.

sentences.zh: 十月，薛道摽突圍，與十餘騎走奔淮西，投常珍奇，薛元寶歸降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xue Daobiao broke the encirclement and with a dozen-odd horsemen fled to Huai west, throwing himself on Chang Zhenqi; Xue Yuanbao returned in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Daobiao broke out with a dozen horsemen, fled west to join Chang Zhenqi, and Yuanbao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉熙太守閻湛之據郡同逆，至是沈靈寵自廬江攻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Administrator of Jinxī, Yan Zhenzhi, had held his commandery in joint rebellion; now Shen Lingchong from Lujiang attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jinxī prefect Yan Zhenzhi had joined the rebellion; Shen Lingchong now attacked him from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 湛之未知尋陽已敗，固守不降。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi did not know Xunyang had already been defeated and held firm without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi, unaware that Xunyang had fallen, held out.

sentences.zh: 靈寵乃取諸將破劉胡文書置車中，攻城偽敗，棄車而走。

translations.literal: Lingchong then took the generals' documents on defeating Liu Hu and placed them in a cart; he feigned defeat in assaulting the city, abandoned the cart, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchong loaded a cart with documents of Liu Hu's defeat, feigned a rout at the walls, and abandoned the cart in flight.

sentences.zh: 湛之得書大駭，其夜奔逃。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi obtained the documents and was greatly terrified; that night he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi read the papers, was terrified, and fled that night.

sentences.zh: 十一月，常珍奇乞降，慮不見納，又求救於索虜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Chang Zhenqi begged to surrender, fearing he would not be accepted, and also begged rescue from the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chang Zhenqi offered to surrender but, fearing refusal, also called on the northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 太宗即以珍奇為司州刺史，領汝南、新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: Taizong at once made Zhenqi Inspector of Si with concurrent charge as Administrator of Runan and Xincai commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong immediately confirmed Zhenqi as Si inspector and prefect of Runan and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 虜亦遣偽帥張窮奇騎萬匹救之。

translations.literal: The barbarians also sent their false commander Zhang Qiongqi with ten thousand horse to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei also sent their general Zhang Qiongqi with ten thousand cavalry to his aid.

sentences.zh: 十二月，虜至汝南，珍奇開門納虜，淮西七縣民並連營南奔，劉順亦棄虜歸順。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the barbarians reached Runan; Zhenqi opened the gates and admitted them; the people of seven Huai west counties all joined camps and fled south; Liu Shun also abandoned the barbarians and returned to submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Wei reached Runan; Zhenqi admitted them; seven Huai-west counties fled south in bands; Liu Shun also abandoned the Wei and submitted.

sentences.zh: 南賊降者，太宗並送琰城下，令與城內交言，由是人情沮喪。

translations.literal: Southern rebels who surrendered were all sent by Taizong below Yan's walls to let them speak with those inside; on this account men's spirits were broken.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong paraded southern defectors before the walls to speak with the garrison, and morale inside collapsed.

sentences.zh: 琰將降，先送休祐內人出城，然後開門。

translations.literal: When Yan was about to surrender, he first sent Xiuyou's household out of the city, then opened the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, about to surrender, first sent out Xiuyou's family, then opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 時琰有疾，以板自輿，與諸將帥面縛請罪。

translations.literal: At that time Yan was ill; he was carried on a board-litter by himself, and with the generals and commanders came out with faces bound to beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was ill and was carried on a litter; he and his officers came out bound to beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 勔並撫宥，無所誅戮，自將帥以下，財物資貨，皆以還之，纖毫無所失。

translations.literal: Liu Yan comforted and pardoned them all, executing none; from commanders down, goods and valuables were all returned—not the slightest thing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan pardoned them all without executions and returned every item of property down to the last scrap.

sentences.zh: 虜騎救琰，至師水，聞城陷，乃破義陽，殺掠數千人而去。

translations.literal: Barbarian horse came to rescue Yan, reached Shishui, heard the city had fallen, then broke Yiyang, killed and plundered several thousand, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cavalry marching to relieve Yan reached Shishui, learned the city had fallen, sacked Yiyang, killed thousands, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 垣式寶尋復反叛，投常珍奇。

translations.literal: Yuan Shibao before long rebelled again and threw himself on Chang Zhenqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shibao soon rebelled again and joined Chang Zhenqi.

sentences.zh: 以平琰功，劉懷珍封艾縣侯，食邑四百戶，垣閎樂鄉縣侯，孟次陽攸縣子，王廣之蒲圻縣子，陳顯達彭澤縣子，呂安國鍾武縣子，食邑各三百戶，黃回葛陽縣男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Yan, Liu Huaizhen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ai county with four hundred households' revenue; Yuan Hong as Marquis of Lexiang county; Meng Ciyang as Viscount of You county; Wang Guangzhi as Viscount of Puqi county; Chen Xianda as Viscount of Pengze county; Lü Anguo as Viscount of Zhongwu county, each with three hundred households' revenue; Huang Hui as Baron of Geyang county with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Yan, Huaizhen was made Marquis of Ai with four hundred households; Hong Marquis of Lexiang; Ciyang Viscount of You; Guangzhi Viscount of Puqi; Xianda Viscount of Pengze; Anguo Viscount of Zhongwu, each with three hundred households; Hui Baron of Geyang with two hundred.

sentences.zh: 送琰及偽節還京都。

translations.literal: Yan and the false insignia were sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the rebel insignia were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫求忠臣必於孝子之門，蓋以類得之也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In seeking loyal ministers one must go to the gate of filial sons—for by kind one obtains them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Loyal ministers are sought among filial sons, for like draws like.

sentences.zh: 昔啟方說主，跡表遺親，鄧攸淳行，愛兼猶子，雖稟分參差，情紀難一，而均薄等厚，未之或偏。

translations.literal: Formerly Qi Fang persuaded his lord and his tracks showed abandonment of kin; Deng You's pure conduct extended love equally to his nephew's son—though endowed portions differed and feeling's rule was hard to unify, they balanced thin and equal thick and were never partial.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fang won his ruler's favor yet abandoned his kin; Deng You was pure in conduct and loved his nephew as a son—though gifts differed and feelings were uneven, they still strove for fairness.

sentences.zh: 惠開親禮雖篤，弟隙尤著，方寸之內，孝友異情，險於山川，有驗於此也。

translations.literal: Huikai's kin courtesy was though thick, yet estrangement from his brothers was especially marked; within a square inch, filial and brotherly feelings differed—more treacherous than mountains and rivers; here is proof of it.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was dutiful in ceremony toward kin, yet his rift with his brothers was glaring; within one breast filial piety and brotherly love pulled apart—more impassable than mountains—and this chapter proves it.
